messages:
erin: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — wanted to consolidate action owners/timelines for the missing spans + aggregation drift stuff. I'll drop what I have and we can update inline.

alex: SG. Can we call out which ETL jobs are still flaky? I have context on the kafka->staging lag ones.

maria: The main problems I saw: 1) span extractor backpressure when downstream GC spikes, 2) nightly aggregator double-count for retried batches, 3) a small window where TTL cleanup deletes un-acked pointers.

erin: Right — here's the working list I sketched (short):
- A: span extractor backpressure -> owner: alex -> mitigation: increase consumer concurrency + add backpressure metric -> ETA: 2 days for mitigation, 2 weeks for full fix.
- B: retries causing double-count in aggregator -> owner: maria -> mitigation: idempotency key + dedupe window -> ETA: patch in 4 days, rollout canary next week.
- C: TTL cleanup race -> owner: sam -> mitigation: introduce lease/checkpoint + revert cleanup window -> ETA: quick revert today, proper fix in 1 week.

dave: Can we add an on-call rotation for these fixes? If someone is OOO we need a clear backup. I can be backup for A this week.

erin: Thanks dave. I'm scheduling daily 15m sync for the next 3 days at 09:15 so we can unblock fast.

alex: For A — dev notes: consumer lag spikes when heap pressure > 1.2GB, GC pauses coincide. Quick mitigation: bump heap and pin GC flags, but that's a band-aid. I'll push config change to staging now.

infra-bot: deploy started by alex:infra at 1834506842 — span-extractor: bump-heap-config -> staging

maria: For B — the dedupe window needs to be keyed by (trace_id, span_id, batch_id). I'll PR the dedupe cache + add a metric `agg.dedupe.hits`. If hits stay low we can lower retention.

sam: TTL revert done -> reverted cleanup job to previous window at 1834506900. Observability alerted and logs show no further deletes for the last 5m.

erin: Nice. Action items and owners updated:
- alex: quick mitigation deployed to staging, verify latency+gc metrics -> due EOD
- alex (full fix): redesign consumer backpressure handling -> due 2026-04-07
- maria: PR for dedupe logic + metric -> PR by 2026-03-30, canary 2026-04-01
- sam: full TTL fix with lease -> due 2026-03-31
- dave: backup owner for A this week, take handover if alex is blocked

dave: I'll shadow alex on the staging run and validate GC traces.

alex: Quick note: this pattern (consumer GC -> missing KV chunks) has happened twice now (see the Feb cluster incident). We should add a recurring regression test to our chaos suite to force short GC pauses and assert no span loss.

erin: Agreed. New item: add GC pause regression test to chaos-suite -> owner: maria -> ETA 2 weeks.

maria: Putting it on my board. Also proposing a weekly observability digest that highlights `agg.dedupe.hits`, `span.kv.misses`, `etl.lag_95` so we spot regressions faster.

erin: Love that. I'll add the digest to weekly eng-ops report and set alerts on sensible thresholds.

alex: One last thing — any customer-facing comms? Support asked if we need a status update.

erin: Small update OK: "We identified and mitigated the root causes of recent span loss and aggregation discrepancies. Engineers are rolling fixes; customers should see improved correctness within 48 hours." I'll craft a short blurb and ping support.

sam: FYI, I've attached logs snippet to the postmortem doc (link) and the TTL revert note.

erin: Great. Let's reconvene tomorrow 09:15. If anyone is blocked ping me directly. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
